about: Captured from v2xw-server on scenarios/scms-audit-mbpipe.yaml at its end (433,033 s): the SCMS metrics catalogue rows, those series binned (every other bin of 240), the run-wide groupings and the Backend snapshot. metrics.spec.ts serves them for the SCMS overview test.

catalogue.definition_md: The share of vehicles whose backend access (cellular coverage, a relaying roadside unit in range) was usable, over the window.

health.caution_note: some vehicles cannot reach the credential backend
health.healthy_note: vehicles can reach the credential backend
health.source: engineering choice
health.unhealthy_note: more than 1 in 10 vehicles cannot reach the credential backend

catalogue.name: backend_link_up
not_accounted: outages shorter than the telemetry window

catalogue.definition_md: Bytes on the wire attributed to the `backend` accounting bucket, divided by the window's length. Invariant I-N1 requires every byte to belong to exactly one bucket.
catalogue.name: bytes_backend
not_accounted: bytes the producer did not attribute to a bucket
physical-layer preamble and padding, unless the producer counts them in bytes_on_wire

catalogue.definition_md: Mean over the window. Certificates each vehicle holds valid at the instant of its security row.

health.caution_note: vehicles are down to a handful of valid pseudonym certificates
health.healthy_note: vehicles hold enough valid pseudonym certificates to keep changing them
health.source: engineering choice: the CAMP SCMS design issues 20 certificates valid per week (Whyte et al., IEEE VNC 2013); fewer than 5 leaves little room for a missed top-up, fewer than 1 cannot sign
health.unhealthy_note: vehicles have run out of valid certificates and cannot sign trusted messages

catalogue.name: cert_pool_valid
not_accounted: certificates preloaded for later periods

catalogue.definition_md: The revocation list's size in bytes as last published.
catalogue.name: crl_bytes
not_accounted: compression on the distribution path
what any individual node holds

catalogue.definition_md: The number of entries in the revocation list as last published.
catalogue.name: crl_entries
not_accounted: what any individual node holds, which lags the published list

catalogue.definition_md: The false-positive rate: `fp / (fp + tn)`.

health.caution_note: above 1 % of honest vehicles are wrongly flagged
health.healthy_note: at most 1 % of honest vehicles are wrongly flagged
health.source: engineering choice; no standard sets a false-positive rate
health.unhealthy_note: above 5 % of honest vehicles are wrongly flagged: revocation would hit them

catalogue.name: det_fpr
not_accounted: the base rate: at a 2 % attacker fraction a 1 % false-positive rate still produces more false than true positives

catalogue.definition_md: Precision: `tp / (tp + fp)`. At the `report` level this is the per-report precision of the legacy `validate.py`; at the `vehicle` level it is `revoked ∩ attacker / revoked`.
catalogue.name: det_precision
not_accounted: the base rate
reports about subjects the run never declared

catalogue.definition_md: Recall, also the true-positive rate: `tp / (tp + fn)`.

health.caution_note: between half and 90 % of attackers are detected
health.healthy_note: at least 90 % of attackers are detected
health.source: engineering choice; no standard sets a detection rate
health.unhealthy_note: fewer than half the attackers are detected

catalogue.name: det_recall
not_accounted: how many reports each detection took
attackers that never acted

catalogue.definition_md: Benign subjects with at least one report (`level = report`) and benign subjects that were revoked (`level = vehicle`).
catalogue.name: false_accusations
not_accounted: how many times each benign subject was reported
a benign subject reported and then cleared, which still counts

catalogue.definition_md: The certificate attachment rate: messages whose signer identifier is a full certificate rather than a digest, divided by all messages.
catalogue.name: full_cert_share
not_accounted: peer-to-peer certificate distribution responses, which carry certificates outside the ordinary message flow
messages whose signer identifier the producer did not record

catalogue.definition_md: Mean over the window. The time between consecutive emitted stages of one revocation (05-protocols.md §8). The stage dimension names the transition, e.g. `decision->issued`.

health.caution_note: a revocation stage takes over a minute
health.healthy_note: each revocation stage completes within a minute
health.source: engineering choice: no standard sets a revocation deadline (IEEE 1609.2.1 and ETSI TS 102 941 leave CRL timing to policy)
health.unhealthy_note: a revocation stage takes over five minutes: a misbehaving vehicle stays trusted

catalogue.name: revocation_latency_stage
not_accounted: stages a protocol does not emit, which invariant I-P4 reports
per-node enforcement spread: this is the transition's distribution, not t95
